rounds.text: Cospower Engineering Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, evidenced by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 2,888 per share against its current market price of Rs 2,147, offering a 25.7% margin of safety [E42, E43]. This valuation discount exists despite extraordinary financial performance, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 768% and sales growth of 287% [E17, E21]. Furthermore, the company boasts exceptional capital efficiency with a return on equity of 39.8% and return on capital employed of 38.2%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. The underlying operational strength is further reinforced by a rules-based screen scoring a high-confidence 93 out of 100 driven by stellar YoY sales and net profit increases [E63, E64, E66]. Momentum is fully aligned with these fundamentals, as demonstrated by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a price sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47, E48]. Conceded: [E2, E33, E60].

Cospower Engineering Ltd trades at a rich valuation that leaves little margin for error, with a P/E of 30.3x and a price-to-book ratio of 8.35x against a book value of ₹ 257 [E1, E2]. These valuation multiples significantly outpace sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E stands at 23.87x and the sector P/B sits at 2.61x [E6, E7]. Furthermore, the stock provides a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], offering no income return to compensate investors for entering at the absolute peak of its 52-week range [E5]. Beneath the headline growth figures, cash generation has turned alarmingly negative, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -15 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -18 Cr in March 2026, leading to a distressed cash conversion ratio of -1.15x [E33, E34, E35]. This cash drain is accompanied by rising borrowings, which increased to Rs 28 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 18 Cr a year earlier [E38], alongside deteriorating working capital metrics as debtor days stretched from 115 to 142 days and working capital days worsened from 81.8 to 125 days [E61, E62]. Operational risks are further compounded by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margin trend over the last two periods [E31, E32], insider dilution through promoter holdings falling to 60.01% in March 2026 from 73.33% in September 2020 [E40], and extreme annualised volatility of 70.5% [E51]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong historical profit growth and return on equity metrics along with positive sectoral tailwinds [E19, E27, E71].

Conceded: the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. However, the rich valuation multiples of 30.3x P/E and 8.35x P/B [E1, E2] are fully justified by elite operational performance, including a stellar 39.8% ROE and 38.2% ROCE that vastly outperform sector medians [E9, E10, E13]. While borrowings rose to Rs 28 Cr [E38], the company commands an exceptional rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 driven by extraordinary triple-digit growth metrics like a 287% TTM sales surge and 768% profit expansion [E17, E21, E63]. The absolute peak 52-week price level [E5] is backed by elite technical strength, with a relative-strength rating of 100 and a rising moving-average alignment [E47, E48]. Furthermore, discounted cash flow modelling proves the stock remains undervalued at Rs 2,147 with a fair intrinsic value of Rs 2,888 and a 25.7% margin of safety [E42, E43], while operating within a powerful Capital Goods sector tailwind [E71].

Conceded: the company features a high rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 alongside strong trailing sales and profit growth [E17, E21, E63]. However, those extraordinary growth metrics sit alongside a severe negative cash conversion of -1.15x, with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -15 Cr and free cash flow dropping to Rs -18 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, the bull's defense of the 8.35x P/B multiple ignores its steep premium over the sector benchmark of 2.61x [E2, E7]. The technical strength and peak 52-week position [E5, E47, E48] are accompanied by an annualised volatility of 70.5% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -47.7% [E50, E51], exposing investors to severe downside risk. Finally, working capital pressures are mounting as debtor days have deteriorated from 115 to 142 days and working capital days have blown out from 81.8 to 125 days [E61, E62], while promoter holdings have steadily eroded down to 60.01% [E40].

Conceded: operating cash flow is negative [E34] and working capital days have increased to 125 [E62], but these are expected frictions for a company scaling with 287% sales growth and 768% profit growth in the last year [E17, E21]. The bear's critique of the P/B ratio [E7] ignores that the company generates an ROE of 39.8% [E13], nearly four times the sector benchmark of 10.59% [E9]. This superior efficiency supports a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 2888, suggesting the current market price provides a 25.7% margin of safety [E42, E43]. While volatility and historical drawdowns are high [E50, E51], they are outweighed by extreme recent outperformance where profit growth has exceeded price growth by 542% [E54], resulting in a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E48]. Finally, the reduction in promoter holding to 60.01% [E40] does not diminish the firm's fundamental strength, as evidenced by a high-confidence rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 [E63] and a strong sector tailwind [E71].

Conceded: the company generates an ROE of 39.8% [E13] and sits in a sector tailwind [E71]. However, dismissing negative operating cash flow of Rs -15 Cr and a cash conversion of -1.15x as mere scaling friction ignores severe liquidity deterioration [E33, E34]. The bull points to a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 2888 [E42], but this projection clashes with the reality of expanding debtor days from 115 to 142 and ballooning working capital requirements to 125 days [E61, E62]. Furthermore, the claim that promoter selling to 60.01% is immaterial [E40] overlooks a significant quarter-on-quarter insider reduction of 5.80% [E60]. Finally, relying on a relative-strength rating of 100 [E48] and a rules-based screen score [E63] fails to justify a price trading at an expensive 8.35x book value [E2] with 70.5% annualized volatility [E51].
